sentences.text:
The brief facts of the case are as follows:
On 09-12-2023 at about 1.45 p.m., the petitioner was riding the motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-02-KF-4802, from Kirloskar cross towards Yashwanthapura circle,
slowly and cautiously, by observing all traffic rules and regulations, on the extreme side of the road.

When he was near Muniswamappa Kalyana Mantap, Tumkur road,
Bengaluru City, at that time the driver of BMTC Bus bearing Reg. No.KA-57-F-4622 came from same direction, in rash and negligent manner, without observing any traffic rules and regulations, endangering to human life and dashed against the motorcycle of the petitioner from behind.
Due to the said impact, the petitioner has fell down on the road and sustained grievous injuries all over the body.
Immediately after the accident, he was shifted to M.S. Ramaiah Hospital, Bengaluru, wherein he took treatment as an in-patient.
Earlier to the accident, he was working as Police Constable and drawing salary of Rs.50,648/- per month.
But, due to the accidental injuries, he has become permanently disabled and thereby lost his earning capacity.
The Yashwanthapura Traffic Police have registered the case against the driver of the said bus for the offences punishable under Section 279 and 337 of I.P.C.
The respondent is the owner of the offending vehicle.
Hence, the respondent is liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Therefore, it is prayed to allow the petition and award compensation of Rs.15,00,000/- with interest.
3. On service of notice to the respondent, the respondent has appeared through his counsel and filed the written statement.
4. The respondent in his written statement has denied all the allegations made in the petition.

He has denied the rashness and negligence on the part of the driver of the BMTC Bus bearing Reg.
No.KA-57-F-4622.
Further, he has denied the age, income and avocation of the petitioner, injuries sustained, medical expenses and treatment taken by him.
Further it is contended that, the compensation claimed is highly excessive and exorbitant.

Further, he has contended that, on 09-12-2023 the BMTC Bus bearing Reg. No.KA-57-F-4622 was proceeding from 31st depot towards Yeshwanthpura, driven by its driver slowly, carefully, on the left side of the road, by observing all the traffic rules and regulations.

When the said bus reached near Muniswamappa Kalyana Mantapa,
Yeshwanthapura, at about 2.00 p.m., one motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-02-KF- 4802, ridden by its rider, in rash and negligent manner, without following traffic rules and regulations, came from same direction on the left side of the BMTC Bus and the right side handle of said motorcycle touched to left back side body of the bus, lost control over his motorcycle and fell down on the left side of the road along with motorcycle and suffered injuries.
The accident has occurred solely due to rash and negligent riding on the petitioner and the driver of the BMTC bus was not at all responsible for the said accident.
But, the petitioner in collusion with the jurisdictional Police has filed a false case against the driver of the said BMTC bus.
Hence, this respondent is not liable to pay any compensation to the petitioner and the claim petition is liable to be dismissed.
Further it is contended that, the petition is bad for non-joinder of necessary parties namely owner and insurance company of the motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-02-KF-4802.
For the above denials and contentions, it is prayed to dismiss the petition.

On the basis of rival pleadings of both the sides, the following issues are framed:
ISSUES 1. Whether the petitioner proves that, he has sustained grievous injuries in the Road Traffic Accident, alleged to have occurred on 09-12-2022 at about 1.45 p.m., near Muniswamy Kalyana Mantapa, Tumkuru Road, Bengaluru, due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the BMTC Bus, bearing registration No. KA-57-F- 4622 ?
2.
Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?

If so, what is the quantum and from whom ?
3. What order or Award ?
6. In order to prove his case, the petitioner has got examined himself as P.W.1 and got marked 24 documents as Ex.P.1 to 24.

Further, he has got examined one more witness namely Dr. Nagaraj B.N.,
as P.W.2.

On the other hand, the respondent has got examined his driver as R.W.1 and got marked 3 documents as Ex.R.1 to 3.
7.
I have heard the arguments of both the sides and perused the entire material placed on record.

8. My findings on the above issues are as under:
Issue No.1: Affirmative Issue No.2: Partly Affirmative Issue No.3: As per the final order, for the following:
REASONS 9. Issue No.1: It is specific case of the petitioner that, on 09-12-2023 at about 1.45 p.m., when he was riding the motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-02-KF-4802, from Kirloskar cross towards Yashwanthapura circle, slowly and cautiously, by observing all traffic rules and regulations, on the extreme side of the road, near Muniswamappa Kalyana Mantap, Tumkur road, Bengaluru City, at that time the driver of offending BMTC Bus bearing Reg. No.KA-57-F-4622 came from same direction, in rash and negligent manner, without observing any traffic rules and regulations and dashed against the motorcycle of the petitioner from behind.
Due to the said impact, the petitioner has fell down on the road and sustained grievous injuries all over the body.

Further it is contended that, earlier to the accident, he was working as Police Constable and drawing salary of Rs.50,648/-
per month.
But, due to the accidental injuries, he has become permanently disabled and thereby lost his earning capacity.
10. In order to prove his case, the petitioner has examined himself as P.W.1 by filing examination-in-chief affidavit, wherein he has reiterated entire averments made in the petition.

Further, in support of his oral evidence, the petitioner has got marked total 23 documents as Ex.P.1 Siddanna vs B.M.T.C on 3 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/24086086/
3 to 23.

Out of the said documents, Ex.P.1 is true copy of F.I.R., Ex.P.2 is true copy of first information statement, Ex.P.3 is true copy of MLC intimation, Ex.P.4 is true copy of sketch, Ex.P.5 is true copy of spot mahazar, Ex.P.6 is true copy of statement of witness, Ex.P.7 is true copy of notice under Section 133 of Motor Vehicles Act, Ex.P.8 and 9 are true copy of reply to notice issued under Section 133 of Motor Vehicles Act (total 2), Ex.P.10 is true copy of Trip sheet of BMTC, Ex.P.11 is true copy of statement of accused, Ex.P.12 is true copy of statement of bus conductor, Ex.P.13 is true copy of wound certificate, Ex.P.14 is true copy of Motor Vehicles Accident report, Ex.P.15 is true copy of registration certificate, Ex.P.16 is true copy of vehicle particulars, Ex.P.17 is discharge summary,
Ex.P.18 is certified copy of photos of BMTC bus (total 2), Ex.P.19 are X-rays (total 4), Ex.P.20 are medical bills (total 62), Ex.P.21 is notarized copy of Department Identity card, Ex.P.22 is Clinical note, Ex.P.23 is X-ray and Ex.P.24 is charge-sheet.

11. On meticulously going through the police documents marked as Ex.P.1 to 16 and 24, prima-facia it reveals that, the accident in question has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending BMTC Bus bearing Reg. No.KA-57-F-4622 and dashing the same to the motorcycle bearing No.KA-02-KF-4802 of the petitioner.

Further it reveals that, due to said impact,
the petitioner has fell down on the road and sustained grievous injuries on his hand and legs.

The investigation officer in his final report/charge-sheet, marked as Ex.P.24, has clearly stated that, the said accident has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending BMTC Bus bearing Reg. No.KA-57-F-4622 and the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries in the said accident.

12. At the outset, it is pertinent to note that, there is no dispute with regard date, time and place of accident, involvement of offending BMTC Bus bearing Reg. No.KA-57- F-4622 in the alleged accident.

But, the respondent has denied the above averred facts and circumstances of the accident and has taken specific defence that, the accident in question has occurred due to sole rash and negligent riding on the part of the petitioner himself and there was no fault on the part of the driver of the BMTC Bus.

Further it is contended that, at the time of alleged accident, the BMTC Bus bearing Reg. No.KA-57-F-4622 was proceeding from 31st depot towards Yeshwanthpura, driven by its driver slowly, carefully, on the left side of the road, by observing all the traffic rules and regulations and when the said bus reached near Muniswamappa Kalyana Mantapa,
Yeshwanthapura, the petitioner being the rider of motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-02-KF-4802,
rode the same in rash and negligent manner on the left side of BMTC Bus and touched the right side handle of his motorcycle to the left back side body of the said bus, lost control over his motorcycle and fell down on the left side of the road along with motorcycle and suffered injuries.
Further it is contended that, the petitioner in collusion with the jurisdictional Police has filed a false case against the driver of the said BMTC Bus.
But, the respondent has failed to establish the said contentions.

Except the self serving statements of R.W.1, who is none other than the accused/driver of offending bus, there is absolutely no other corroborative oral or documentary evidence produced by the respondent to show that, the accident in question has occurred due to sole rash and negligent riding of the motorcycle by the petitioner himself and there was no fault on the part of the driver of offending BMTC bus and the same has been falsely implicated in the said accident by the petitioner.

Siddanna vs B.M.T.C on 3 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/24086086/
4

On the other hand, the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner clearly establishes that, the said accident has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending BMTC Bus bearing Reg. No.KA-57-F-4622 and dashing the same to the motorcycle of the petitioner from back side and the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries to his hand and legs in the said accident.
The evidence of P.W.1 is fully corroborated with the documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner.

Though the learned counsel for respondent cross-examined P.W.1 in length, nothing worth has been elicited from his mouth which creates doubt on the veracity of his evidence or which establishes that, the said accident has taken place due to rash and negligent riding of the petitioner himself or there was any contributory negligence on his part in the cause of accident.

13. The Ex.P.4 spot sketch and Ex.P.5 spot mahazar also clearly speaks that, the said accident has taken place in the middle of Bengaluru-Tumkuru road, near Muniswamappa Kalyana Mantapa,
Bengaluru city, due to dashing of offending BMTC Bus bearing Reg. No. KA-57-F-4622 to the ongoing motorcycle of the petitioner bearing Reg. No.KA- 02-KF-4802.
Further, as per the Motor Vehicles Accident Report, which is marked as Ex.P.14, the accident is not caused due to any mechanical defects in the vehicles involved in the accident.

When the accident was not caused due to any mechanical defects in the vehicles involved in the accident and there was no rash and negligent riding on the part of the petitioner/rider of the motorcycle, then in the present facts and circumstances of the case it can be presumed that, the said accident had occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending BMTC bus.

Further, the investigation officer has clearly stated in his final report/charge-sheet that, the accident in question has occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending BMTC Bus bearing Reg. No.KA-57-F-4622 and dashing the same to the motorcycle of the petitioner.
Admittedly the said charge-sheet has not been challenged by the driver or owner of the offending BMTC Bus bearing Reg. No.KA-57-F-4622.

In such circumstances, there is no impediment to believe the final report filed by the investigation officer and other police records, regarding the date, time and place of accident, involvement of the offending BMTC bus in the accident, rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending vehicle and injuries caused to the petitioner in the said accident.

14. Further, on meticulously going through the Ex.P.13 wound certificate, Ex.P.17 discharge summary, Ex.P.19 x- rays (total 4), Ex.P.22 clinical note and Ex.P.23 x-ray, it clearly reveals that, the petitioner has suffered grievous injuries in a road traffic accident.
As per the said documents, the petitioner has suffered right humerus mid shaft comminuted fracture with fracture of the right base of the 1st metacarpal fracture.
The same has been deposed by P.W.2, who is the doctor who has examined the petitioner for the purpose of assessment of disability suffered by him.
On the other hand, there is no rebuttal evidence produced by the respondent to show that, the above medical records are false documents.
There is nothing on record to disbelieve the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner.

Therefore, in such circumstances and in the light of above observations, it can safely be held that, the respondent has failed to rebut the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner regarding the rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending BMTC Bus bearing Reg. No.KA-57-F-4622 and the injuries caused to the petitioner in the said accident.

Further, it is well settled principle of law that, in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims,
the claimants are not required to prove the case as required to be done in a criminal trial.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Parameshwari V/s Amir Chand and others, reported in (2011)
SCC 635, has clearly held that, "in a road accident claim cases the strict principle of proof in a criminal case are not required."

SCC 635

sentences.text: 16. The Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the case of Bimla Devi and others V/s Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others, reported in (2009) 13 SCC 513, has clearly held that, "in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims, the claimants are merely required to establish their case on touch stone of preponderance of probability and the standard of proof on beyond reasonable doubt could not be applied."

Therefore, in the light of observations made in the above cited decisions and for the above stated reasons, this Court is of the considered opinion that, the petitioner has successfully proved that, he has sustained grievous injuries in a motor vehicle accident, occurred on 09-12-2023 at about 1.45 p.m., near Muniswamappa Kalyana Mantapa, Tumkuru Road, Bengaluru City, due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending BMTC Bus bearing Reg. No.KA-57-F-4622.
Hence, I answer Issue No.1 in Affirmative.
18. Issue No.2:

While answering the above issue this Court has come to conclusion that, the petitioner has successfully proved that, the accident has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending BMTC Bus, bearing Reg. No.KA-57-F-4622 and he has sustained grievous injuries in the said accident.
The medical records placed on record clearly speaks that, the petitioner has sustained right humerus mid shaft comminuted fracture with fracture of the right base of the 1st metacarpal fracture.
Therefore, this Court is of the further opinion that, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under various heads.

The damages are to be assessed under two heads i.e. pecuniary damages, such as medical treatment, attendants, transport, actual loss of earning,
future loss of earning etc., and non-pecuniary damages, such as mental and physical shock, loss of amenities, loss of expectation of life, loss of prospects of marriage etc.

The petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads:
i) Towards loss of future income:
In order to determine the compensation towards loss of future income, the age, monthly income and disability of the petitioner are to be determined.
To prove his age, the petitioner has not produced any relevant document.
In the petition, his age is shown as 26 years, as on the date of accident.
Likewise, in all the medical records, produced and got marked by the petitioner as Ex.P.13, 17 and 19, his age is mentioned as 26 years.
Further, the petitioner has deposed in his examination-in-chief affidavit that, at the time of accident his age was 26 years.
On the other hand, the age of the petitioner is not specifically denied by the respondent in its written statement and even not seriously disputed in the cross-examination of the petitioner.
Even, there is no contrary material on record, to disbelieve the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner.

sentences.text: Therefore, in such circumstances, there is no impediment to consider the age of the petitioner as 26 years, as on the date of accident.

a) Further, the P.W.2, who is the doctor who has examined the petitioner for the purpose of assessment of disability, has clearly deposed in his examination-in-chief affidavit that, on clinical examination he found that, the petitioner has suffered right humerus mid shaft comminuted fracture with fracture of the right base of the 1st metacarpal fracture.

Further he has deposed that,
on clinical and radiological examination of injuries caused to the petitioner he found that, there is 45% permanent physical disability of the right arm and 15% permanent physical disability to the whole body of the petitioner.

Further, the Ex.P.13 wound certificate, Ex.P.17 discharge summary,
Ex.P.19 x-rays (total 4), Ex.P.22 clinical note and Ex.P.23 x-ray clearly speaks that, the petitioner had sustained the above stated injuries and he has undergone surgery.
Though, the learned counsel for respondent has cross-examined P.W.2 in length, nothing worth has been elicited from his mouth which creates doubt on the veracity of his evidence.
Further, he has clearly denied the suggestions made to him that, there is no disability to the petitioner and he has exaggerated the percentage of disability to the petitioner.

But, it is pertinent to note that, the P.W.2 has deposed in his evidence that, the accident has occurred on 09-12-2023 and he has assessed the disability to the petitioner on 07-07-2025, which is after lapse of one year and six months from the date of injuries caused to the petitioner.
Further he has stated that, the petitioner requires one more surgery for removal of implants.
This clearly goes to show that, the disability has been assessed before the completion of full treatment to the petitioner.
As per the gazette notification issued by the Ministry of Social Justice of Government of India, the disability should be assessed after completion of treatment.

entities.text: Ministry of Social Justice of Government of India
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: If the disability had been assessed after future surgery, perhaps there would have been reduction in the percentage of the disability.

Further, it is pertinent to note that, P.W.2 has clearly stated in his cross-examination that, he has assessed only physical disability and not functional disability,
fractures are united, implants are in situ, after removal of implants the range of movements will vary and the petitioner can perform his day to day activities with some difficulties.

Therefore, taking into consideration the age of the petitioner, injuries sustained, avocation of the petitioner, duration of treatment and oral and documentary evidence on record, this Court is of the opinion that,
considering the disability of 10% to the whole body of the petitioner would be justified
. Hence, in the instant case the disability of 10% to the whole body of the petitioner is considered.
b) The petitioner has deposed in his evidence that, before accident he was working as Police Constable and drawing salary of Rs.50,648/- per month.
Further, he has deposed that, due to grievous injuries suffered in the said accident he is unable to do his work.
The respondent has specifically denied the same.
In such circumstances, the burden was on the petitioner to prove his avocation and income.

To substantiate the same, he has produced copy of Department Identity card,
which is marked as per Ex.P.21.
But, he has not produced any document to show that, before accident he was drawing salary of Rs.50,648/- per month.
On the other hand, he has clearly admitted in his cross-examination that, even today he is working in the Police Department.

This clearly goes to show that, the petitioner is continued in the same job and doing the same work as he was doing before the accident and the disability suffered by him has not affected his routine work or avocation.
There is no loss of income to the petitioner, due to injuries sustained in the accident.

Therefore, in such circumstances, the question of awarding compensation for loss of future income Siddanna vs B.M.T.C on 3 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/24086086/
7 due to permanent disability suffered by him does not arise at all.

sentences.text:
For the disability suffered by him,
the petitioner may get compensation under the head loss of amenities and discomfort, but not under the head loss of future income due to disability.
Hence, this Court is of the opinion that, the petitioner is not entitled for compensation under this particular head.

ii) Medical expenses: The petitioner has deposed that, he has incurred expenses of Rs.3,00,000/-
towards medical, conveyance, nourishment and other incidental charge etc.
In order to prove the same, he has produced 62 medical bills, as per Ex.P.20.
But, the P.W.1 has clearly admitted in his cross-examination that, his medical expenses are borne by his department.
Further, though the petitioner has deposed in his evidence that, he has spent Rs.30,000/- out of his own pocket, towards his medical expenses, he has not produced any document to establish the same.

Therefore, in such circumstances, considering that the entire medical expenses of the petitioner has been reimbursed by his department, this Court is of the opinion that, the petitioner is not entitled for any compensation under the head of medical expenses.
iii) Pain and sufferings:
In the present case, the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries i.e. right humerus mid shaft comminuted fracture with fracture of the right base of the 1st metacarpal fracture.
As per Ex.P.17 discharge summary
, the petitioner has taken treatment as in-patient for 8 days from 27-12-2023 to 03-01-2024, in M.S. Ramaiah Hospital, Bengaluru.

Further, as per P.W.2,
the said injury has caused physical disability to the petitioner.
In such circumstances, certainly the petitioner might have suffered pain and sufferings.

Therefore, taking into considering the injuries sustained and disability to the petitioner, this Court is of the opinion that, compensation amount of Rs.50,000/- is to be awarded to the petitioner towards pain and sufferings.
iv) Attendant charges:
As per Ex.P.17 discharge summary, the petitioner has taken treatment as in-patient for 8 days in M.S. Ramaiah Hospital, Bengaluru.
He might have spent considerable amount towards attendant charges during that period.

Therefore, compensation of Rs.1000 x 8 =
Rs.8,000/- is awarded towards the attendant charges.
v) Food and nourishment:
As per Ex.P.17 discharge summary, the petitioner has taken treatment as in-patient for 8 days in M.S. Ramaiah Hospital, Bengaluru.
He might have spent considerable amount towards food and nourishment during that period.

Therefore, compensation of Rs.800 x 8 =
Rs.6,400/- is awarded towards food and nourishment charges.
vi) Conveyance expenses:

The petitioner is the resident of Goudgaon, Koganoor, Gulbarga, the accident has taken place near Muniswamappa Kalyana Mantapa, Tumkuru Road, Bengaluru City and the petitioner has taken treatment at M.S. Ramaiah Hospital, Bengaluru.
Taking into consideration the distance in between the place of accident and the place of treatment

,
compensation of Rs.10,000/- is awarded towards conveyance.
vii) Loss of income during treatment period:

The petitioner has clearly admitted in his cross-examination that, at present he is continued working in the Police Department and he has not produced any document to show that he has not attended the work for 3 months or he has not been paid salary during the treatment period.

Therefore, in such circumstances, the question of awarding Siddanna vs B.M.T.C on 3 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/24086086/
8 compensation for loss of income during treatment period does not arise at all.

entities.text: Siddanna vs B.M.T.C on 3 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Hence, this Court is of the opinion that, the petitioner is not entitled for compensation under this particular head.
viii) Loss of amenities:

It is evident from the documents placed on record that, as on the date of accident the age of the petitioner was 26 years and unfortunately he has suffered right humerus mid shaft comminuted fracture with fracture of the right base of the 1st metacarpal fracture.
Further, he has suffered permanent disability to the extent of 10% to the whole body.
Therefore, awarding compensation of Rs.40,000/- towards loss of amenities would be just and reasonable.
ix) Future medical expenses:
The P.W.2 has clearly deposed in his evidence that, the petitioner needs to undergo one more surgery for removal of implants the estimate of this surgery is around Rs.60,000/-.
But, admittedly the P.W.2 has not issued estimation of cost for the said surgery or for further treatment.
Therefore, this Court is of the opinion that, awarding compensation of Rs.20,000/- towards future medical expenses would be just and reasonable.

19. Accordingly, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under different heads as follows:
1. Loss of future income Nil 2.
Medical expenses Nil 3. Pain and sufferings Rs. 50,000-00 4. Attendant charges 8,000-00 5. Food and nourishment 6,400-00 6.
Conveyance expenses 10,000-00 7. Loss of income during Nil treatment period 8. Loss of amenities 40,000-00
9. Future medical expenses 20,000-00 Total Rs. 1,34,400-00

In all, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.1,34,400/- with interest at the rate of 6% per annum (excluding interest on future medical expenses of Rs.20,000/-), from the date of petition till its realization.
20. Liability:
Admittedly, as on the date of accident, the respondent is the owner of the offending vehicle.

Further, the evidence placed on record by the petitioner clearly establishes that, due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending BMTC bus bearing Reg. No. KA-57-F- 4622 the accident has occurred and the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries in the said accident.
In such circumstances, the respondent being the owner of offending vehicle is vicariously liable to compensate for the damage caused by the usage of said vehicle.

Therefore, for the above stated Siddanna vs B.M.T.C on 3 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/24086086/
9 reasons, holding that, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.1,34,400/-, with interest at the rate of 6% per annum (excluding interest on future medical expenses of Rs.20,000/-), from the date of petition till its realization, from the respondent, I answer Issue No.2 in Partly Affirmative.
21. Issue No.3:
In view of the above findings, I proceed to pass the following order:
ORDER The petition is partly allowed with costs.

The petitioner is entitled to compensation of Rs.1,34,400/- (Rupees one lakh thirty four thousand and four hundred only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., (excluding interest on future medical expenses of Rs.20,000/-) from the date of petition till realisation.
The respondent is liable to pay the above compensation amount to the petitioner and it is directed to pay the said amount within two months from the date of this order.
The entire compensation amount with proportionate interest shall be released in favour of the petitioner through e-payment on proper identification and verification.
Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.2,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.

Further, it is well settled principle of law that, in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims,
the claimants are not required to prove the case as required to be done in a criminal trial.
The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Parameshwari V/s Amir Chand and others, reported in (2011)
SCC 635, has clearly held that, "in a road accident claim cases the strict principle of proof in a criminal case are not required."
16. The Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the case of Bimla Devi and others V/s Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others, reported in (2009) 13 SCC 513, has clearly held that, "in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims, the claimants are merely required to establish their case on touch stone of preponderance of probability and the standard of proof on beyond reasonable doubt could not be applied."
The damages are to be assessed under two heads i.e. pecuniary damages, such as medical treatment, attendants, transport, actual loss of earning,
future loss of earning etc., and non-pecuniary damages, such as mental and physical shock, loss of amenities, loss of expectation of life, loss of prospects of marriage etc.
